stem: A client has a documented immediate hypersensitivity reaction to sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim. A new prescription for sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim is entered. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Administer the prescribed dose because a prior hypersensitivity reaction does not affect later use of the same medication.
options.B: Administer a reduced first dose because lowering the dose removes the contraindication from prior hypersensitivity.
options.C: Premedicate with an antihistamine and administer the medication because premedication overrides the labeled contraindication.
options.D: Do not administer the medication and clarify the prescription because known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides is a contraindication.

rationale: The current sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim label lists known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides as a contraindication. D is therefore the best nursing action before administration. A ignores the documented contraindication. B is not supported by the label; dose reduction does not remove a hypersensitivity contraindication. C is also unsupported because antihistamine premedication does not negate the labeled contraindication.
educational_objective: Before administering sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, identify documented hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides as a contraindication and clarify the prescription rather than attempting dose reduction or premedication.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_document_title: Sulfamethoxazole and Trimethoprim Tablets — Prescribing Information
source_locator: CONTRAINDICATIONS; WARNINGS — Hypersensitivity and Other Serious or Fatal Reactions; Management of Hypersensitivity and Other Serious Reactions
source_claim_supported: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides; serious hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis can occur.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: Review pertinent data prior to medication administration; Identify client allergies and contraindications; Handle and administer high-risk medications safely
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication allergy and contraindication screening
correction_summary: Replaced the original broad sulfonamide-antibiotic versus nonantibiotic cross-reactivity construct with a directly label-supported medication-safety scenario using the same sulfonamide allergy domain. This avoids relying on a specialty-society generalization where the required pharmacology hierarchy favors DailyMed/FDA. The final item tests the explicit sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim hypersensitivity contraindication and uses only label-adjudicable alternatives.

audit_findings.option_D: Correct — do not administer and clarify because the medication is contraindicated with known hypersensitivity.
